subject: Orbis: retention carveout and ephemeral-log purge coordination
messages:
From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@orbishealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Ops <secops@orbishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: clarify retention of backups and ephemeral logs for Orbis integration

Hi Chloe —

Quick one from our compliance team as we finalize the integration checklist: can you confirm Redwood's retention and deletion behaviour for two items we track closely: (1) backups/snapshots that include customer data and (2) ephemeral inference logs (request/response KV caches, debug logs). Our DPA currently says backups are retained for 90 days by default but the engineering team at Orbis needs to know if there are any short-term exceptions or staggered purge windows that could affect incident forensics.

Specifically:
- Is there a documented purge cadence for snapshots that may include customer payloads?
- Do you support short-term audit copies that outlive normal retention (e.g., 180-day carveouts) under an approved exception?
- For ephemeral logs, is there an automatic truncation or is it tied to a rolling TTL per subprocessor?

We may need a brief note for our DPO and Security Ops; happy to take a short call if easier.

Thanks —
Ellen
Ellen Shaw
Senior Compliance Manager, Orbis Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: clarify retention of backups and ephemeral logs for Orbis integration

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the clear ask. I'll loop in ops for details but to set expectations: our standard backup retention window is 90 days, snapshots are included in that window, and ephemeral inference logs are retained for 30 days by default, with configurable TTLs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Before I send a formal write-up for your DPO, two clarifying items would help:
1) Do you need an audit copy that must be retained beyond 90 days (e.g., 180 days) for regulatory reasons? If so, is that per-customer or per-incident?
2) Are you asking about long-term forensic exports (paper trail) or an operational exception for investigation-only access?

Marissa and Laura — can you confirm whether we can provide a short-term (180d) exception and what the operational cost / subprocessor implications would be? Also looping Markus for the purge timing detail so Orbis knows how staged deletes look from a restore perspective.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: clarify retention of backups and ephemeral logs for Orbis integration

Chloe / team —

Technical notes for Orbis:
- Backup snapshots: exported and internal snapshots live in object storage with lifecycle rules that transition to cold storage at 30 days and are scheduled for final purge at 90 days. Purge jobs run in a staggered daily window (02:00–04:00 UTC) per cluster to avoid cross-region spike.
- Exception handling: we can create an "audit copy" hold for a given customer that marks snapshots as non-expiring for up to 180 days; this is a manual workflow that requires approvals (Legal signoff + a ticket to SRE). Operational caveat: creating an audit copy increases storage costs and may require transient access to subprocessor-managed buckets in certain regions.
- Ephemeral logs / request traces: default TTL 30 days; we support downsampling (token-level redaction + 7-day hot window + 23-day cold window) for Hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private, TTLs can be configured by customer policy.
- Restore profile: restores from snapshot are possible within the retention window; if an audit copy is created the snapshot is flagged and excluded from the purge job but still follows the same restore verification steps (integrity checks, SRE approval).

Attachments: backup-retention-matrix.csv (showing per-region TTL and subprocessor buckets), log-rotation-diagram.png, proposed-canary-schedule.xlsx (draft of a staged purge cadence we can offer as an option).

Suggested next steps for Orbis:
1) Confirm whether you need a per-incident preserve or a per-customer 180d audit copy.
2) If yes, we'll prepare a DPA addendum language (Legal) and outline subprocessor notices where cross-border storage is affected.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@orbishealth.com>

Subject: Re: Request: clarify retention of backups and ephemeral logs for Orbis integration

Thanks Markus — that's helpful.

Short answer: our DPO prefers a per-incident preserve for now (we have occasional legal holds that require 6-month availability), but a per-customer 180d audit copy could be acceptable if we can place strong access controls and have the subprocessor cross-border map.

Couple follow-ups:
- Can you list which subprocessors would be touched if we request a 180d audit copy (we need the list for our vendor roster)?
- For per-incident preserves, what is the SLA for snapshot marking and how do we trigger it? Ideally we'd like a 48-hour cutoff from the request to mark the copy.

Happy to take a 30-minute sync next week if that helps accelerate.

—Ellen
Ellen Shaw
Senior Compliance Manager, Orbis Health

Ellen —

Appreciate the quick turn. Proposed plan below so it's in writing for your DPO & Security Ops:

Action plan (Redwood):
- Per-incident preserve: SRE will accept a ticket from your Security Ops mailbox; requested preserves will be acknowledged within 24 hours and marked within 48 hours. We will provide a ticket link and an expected completion timestamp.
- 180d audit copy: available as a scoped DPA addendum. We'll draft amendment language that includes: host-region mapping, subprocessor disclosure (list), access controls (RBAC + KMS restrictions), and storage cost responsibilities.
- Subprocessors: Laura will compile the current subprocessor list and mark which regions would be engaged for the audit copy (expect that to be with our object-storage provider and the edge caching subprocessor where applicable).
- Canary purge schedule: we'll offer a non-production canary purge schedule for you to validate the erase workflow before expanding to production (reference: proposed-canary-schedule.xlsx).

Next steps for Orbis:
1) Confirm whether you want a per-incident preserve only (we can proceed immediately) or if you prefer to negotiate the 180d addendum.
2) If addendum desired, please loop in Legal and we will open a DocuSign request; I'll include Marissa to drive the contractual path.

I'll escalate this to Legal and Sales to prepare the amendment + subprocessor disclosure; Laura will share the subprocessor list by EOD Tue 15 Jun.

Chloe Martin
